summary.text: A 2-year-old girl presented to an outpatient coagulation clinic with recurrent hematomas (ISTH BAT score 2); thrombocytopathy was suspected on reduced PFA-100 results and she was referred. Her mother reported leukemia of unknown specificity in siblings of the maternal grandparents.

At first presentation she had persistent thrombocytopenia (109–136 G/L), impaired aggregometry with collagen, ADP and epinephrine, and normal platelet size; thrombin-stimulated flow cytometry showed reduced CD62 and CD63 exposure, indicating a combined granule secretion defect.

NGS copy number analysis showed a heterozygous RUNX1 deletion, confirmed by microarray as a 1.56 Mb deletion; it was not found in the parents, the mother had normal counts and the recently born brother lacks it, suggesting a de novo occurrence. Bone marrow aspiration showed no AML or MDS, slightly reduced cellularity and dysplastic megakaryocytes, and regular checkups were recommended.

Table 1 columns were read from span markers: LTA agent and percentage cells, a "Platelets" cell inside the aggregometry group, then flow cytometry; the platelet-count cell is a median or minimum per footnote 1.
Flags low on aggregometry values rely on the Table 1 footnote definition of reduced aggregation (< 60%).
P2.3 age differs between text (30-year-old) and Table 1 (40 y); P4.1 and P4.2 table platelet counts differ from the text ranges; none reconciled.
Several data are "data not shown" (family 4 flow cytometry, CNV in P2.2 and P2.3) and are recorded as stated without values.
Supplement SM1 (Table_1.DOCX) lists gene panel contents only and holds no patient data.
Cohort-level statements, literature comparisons and guideline recommendations in the Discussion are not recorded as patient facts.
